approved: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (Customs Charges Imposition) Bill 2025
Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is one of three in a package that would create a legal basis for charging fees related to the administration of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act 1999.
The specific activities subject to charges and their amounts would be set out in regulations, and the charges would be limited to recovering the Commonwealth's costs.
The bill would apply only to charges classified as customs duties, with separate bills covering excise and general charges, as required by the Constitution.
The bill would impose charges on prescribed matters connected with the EPBC Act.
The bill would limit charges to cost recovery amounts approved by the Minister.
The bill would provide for collection and recovery of charges through amendments to the EPBC Act.
People or entities involved in activities regulated under the EPBC Act that are subject to customs charges.

Moved the second reading of the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation (Customs Charges Imposition) Bill 2025, which would establish cost-recovery charges for prescribed matters connected with administering the Act, with activities and amounts set by regulation after consultation.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders to expedite debate and voting on seven environment bills, including limiting consideration in detail to five minutes per amendment set unless extended by a minister, and moved that the question be put.

Moved procedural motions to suspend standing orders and set the day's business, including immediate consideration of the Environment Protection Reform Bill and related bills, specified times for second reading and remaining stages, permitted divisions after 4.30 pm, and subsequent consideration of listed Senate business.
